subject: Learning Methods
title: Spaced Repetition Basics
description: A short lesson to help you apply Spaced Repetition Basics.

hook.text: Reviewing at expanding intervals beats cramming every time. One hour of spaced review outperforms five hours of massing.

buildup.text: After first learning, review after one day, then three days, then one week, then two weeks.

discovery.text: Each successful retrieval at a longer interval strengthens the memory and extends the time until next review.

twist.text: The review should feel slightly difficult. If it is too easy, you are reviewing too soon.

climax.text: Apps like Anki automate the intervals. But even a simple calendar reminder system works effectively.

punchline.text: Space your reviews. Let forgetting begin, then rescue it.

quiz.question: Why should spaced reviews feel slightly difficult?
options: Difficulty causes stress which helps memory
If retrieval is too easy, you are reviewing too soon
Hard practice takes longer and gives more exposure
